**Results:** First mistakes of the game. Both my answer AND my verdict were wrong. Score: 18/20.

**My task (game patch notes):** I selected 7 records, excluding Moon Dagger, Verdant Bow, and Rift Medic because they lacked explicit patch version mentions. I interpreted "with patch version" as a strict filter requiring an explicit version string in the line itself. But the ground truth apparently includes records where the patch is implied by document context (all balance changes in a patch notes document belong to some patch). The "attributes" listed describe what the records contain overall, not a per-line mandatory token. Lesson: when an extraction instruction lists attributes, don't use their absence as an exclusion criterion unless the instruction explicitly says "must explicitly state."

I should have been more skeptical about whether variable definitions (line 1) truly constitute "constraints that include a relation" vs. just declaring the existence of variables. Lesson: "variable" + "relation" + "value/expression" — a pure variable declaration (L and W exist) lacks the relation and value components.

**What I learned:**
- Don't over-filter on optional-attribute grounds; context can satisfy requirements.
- When checking a partner's answer, don't just confirm your initial read matches theirs — probe edge cases (does a pure variable definition count as a "constraint with a relation"?).

**Lesson:** When uncertain about schema, inspect first — a failed query burns the same 4 credits as inspect but gives you less (inspect also hands back value_domains). A guessed-name query is never cheaper than inspect; it's inspect with a coin-flip multiplier on top.

Blind accept was the 3rd of 4 blind verdicts to land correctly (Ep 1's was the miss).

**Series recap:** 17/20 — correct on 8 of 10 own tasks (Ep 5 over-strict filtering, Ep 10 schema-guessing blowup) and right on 7 of 10 verdicts (Ep 1 blind-accept miss, plus two correct answers Alice rejected in Ep 3 and 9). The 8+4 budget discipline worked whenever I followed it; both losses came from abandoning it. If episodes continued, the rule set was settled: inspect before query, hard-filter exclusions in extraction, verify-then-verdict whenever 4+ credits survive, and transfer only post-verdict.
